reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate and adds shared predicates (isDailyWeekendSkip, isNonBusinessDay) that every site uses, though no shared 'resolve the dates a config falls on' step is extracted.

duplication.why: The 'filter daily weekend/holiday occurrences, then move the rest' pipeline is written out separately in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (and again in getNextDate), and look-ahead padding is computed with two different heuristics.

placement.why: Date rules live in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts as the tree does, but the server handlers still assemble the weekend pipeline themselves.

scope.why: Only schedule date logic, the new handler, types, tests and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: The day-level rules are centralised, but each consumer re-composes skip/move/padding logic, so a future rule change still risks missing a site.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter; getNextDate gained a daily-skip early-return branch; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts each re-implement the filter-then-adjust sequence inline (schedule-template re-adjusts after getNextDate via the inverted noSkipWeekend flag)
